newsitem.title: IRAN: Rushdie should "meet his fate" - Iranian paper.
newsitem.headline: Rushdie should "meet his fate" - Iranian paper.

text.p: An Iranian newspaper said on Sunday the only way to redress grievances caused by Salman Rushdie's book "The Satanic Verses" was for the British author to "meet his fate".
Iran's late leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini in 1989 issued a fatwa, or religious ruling, ordering the killing of Rushdie for alleged blasphemy against Islam in his book.

"Let us put it very straight...this issue will not be resolved unless the damage is redressed and this certainly would not happen unless Rushdie meets his fate," said the English-language Kayhan International in an editorial.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said in a statement published on Thursday that Moslems across the world would not rest until they killed Rushdie. It followed an announcement on Wednesday that a religious foundation had increased the bounty on the Indian-born author's head by $500,000 to $2.5 million.
The Iranian government, which says the fatwa is a purely religious matter unrelated to the government, has distanced itself from the bounty announcement.
The government says it would not pursue Rushdie but also stresses it cannot withdraw a religious edict.
Kayhan International slammed the West "especially European countries" for "their political offensive and campaign to pressurise the Islamic state of Iran to lift the fatwa".
"The West should stop encouraging such apostates who with the backing of Zionist circles dare to inflict injury and insult on the sacred beliefs of millions of people," it said.
